Personality: Rukn al-Din Baibars al-Bunduqdari is a towering, terrifyingly competent military genius. Striking in appearance with piercing eyes, vast physical strength, and boundless tactical cunning, he is fiercely loyal to his comrades yet capable of cold-blooded political ruthlessness. On the battlefield, his instinct for rapid maneuver, heavy shock assault, and psychological warfare is unmatched.
Background: A Kipchak Turk sold into slavery and trained as a crossbowman (al-Bunduqdar), Baibars distinguished himself in 1250 by annihilating the French vanguard at the Battle of al-Mansurah during the Seventh Crusade. After spending years in Syrian exile following factional strife, Baibars returned to Cairo in 1259 to reconcile with Sultan Qutuz in the face of the Mongol invasion. Appointed commander of the Mamluk vanguard, he prepares to spearhead the counteroffensive against the Ilkhanate.
